description:
Board mover, s495, NOT caused by s492c -- measured on both sides:

  base 5ce155cb   PARTIAL 16/14, 190 lines of TAP, then
                  "Heap exhausted during allocation: 19660800 bytes available,
                   42781936 requested"
  s492c tree      the same 42,781,936-byte request fails with 4,784,128 bytes
                  available; the board's cold-cache run produced NO TAP at all
                  (FAIL 0/0), a warm run produced 190 lines like the base

So the file is an OOM case in BOTH trees and the only thing that moved is how
much heap was left when the request came -- the s492c image carries a little
more (a bigger runtime, one more shim).  perl runs the file to completion.

WHAT TO MEASURE FIRST: what asks for 42 MB in one go.  The number is identical
on both sides, so it is one allocation in the program, not fragmentation --
most likely a string or list built by Text::Balanced's extract_multiple over
the test's own input.  A board row whose value depends on heap headroom is
worthless as a regression signal, so this file should either be fixed or
registered (baselines/cpan-board-timeouts.tsv is the existing shape for
"this file's verdict is not stable").


=== OBSERVED AGAIN (s497b resume, 2026-09-27) ===
The CPAN board base (main 1b0baa7c) vs s497b tree: base FAIL 0/0 rc=0, tree PARTIAL 16/14 -- the only board mover, and it is THIS task.  Full-output re-runs of both (s497b worktree scratch/s497b/extmul-main2.full + extmul-tree.full) die identically of Heap exhausted (~95 % of 1 GB) at line 117 extract_multiple(q{$var = "val" && (1,2,3);}) after the same 30 rows; base kept its rows in the full-output run and lost them in both --rows runs.  Headroom, not code.
subject: PRE-EXISTING OOM: Text-Balanced t/05_extmul.t asks for ONE 42 MB allocation and dies -- how many rows it produces depends on heap headroom
